name: Lumiere Blue
lede: Lumiere Blue is a pale grey-green teal on screens, and its name echoes an obscure artificial pigment, bleu lumière, listed in 1901.

sections.title: A pigment name, maybe
sections.body:
The *Pigment Compendium* [1] lists *bleu lumière* as a variant name for a blue. It says Church listed it in 1901 as a new addition, said to be an artificial copper hydrate whose precise composition is unknown [1]. Whether the color name comes from that pigment is undocumented.

The color itself is in the charts. Ridgway's 1912 atlas shows it at plate XX, hue 43', tone d, ISCC-NBS puts it in block 163, and Maerz and Paul's dictionary dates it to 1905 [2]. The dates sit close to the pigment listing, but nothing we hold links the two [1][2]. The swatch is a muted grey-green, nearest to [[ash]] among our learnable names, and not the clean blue the name promises [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 74 (0.31 per cent) hold a color within six units of this swatch over at least five per cent of the canvas [3]. The top three matches are two beach scenes and a view of sailboats, dated 1863 to 1888 [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [3].

origin.named_after: possibly the pigment bleu lumière; undocumented

questions.q: How did the Pigment Compendium describe bleu lumière, listed by Church in 1901?
True or false: our sources show the color Lumiere Blue was named after the pigment bleu lumière.

openers: The pigment bleu lumière was listed in 1901; the color name is not proven to come from it.
